findings.title: Cancel imminent reminders immediately instead of waiting for cron
findings.body: Scheduled emails are now only marked cancelled, even when their send time is before the next 15-minute cron run. For example, cancelling a booking two minutes before its reminder is due leaves the email scheduled in SendGrid until after it has been sent; the cron then deletes the expired database row before attempting cancellation. Reminders near their send time need an immediate cancellation path rather than unconditional deferral.

findings.title: Rescheduling bypasses the deferred cancellation mechanism
findings.body: Rescheduling passes immediateDelete=true for every scheduled email, so cancellations for reminders days in the future still occupy SendGrid's limited pending-cancellation slots until their scheduled dates. This recreates the 100-pending-cancellation failure described in the PR. When that immediate request fails, deleteScheduledEmailReminder only logs the error and never sets cancelled=true, so the cron cannot retry it and the old booking's reminder is still sent. Rescheduling needs the same durable, deferred cancellation mechanism as booking cancellation, except where immediate cancellation is necessary.

findings.title: Persist successful cancellations before processing the next reminder
findings.body: Database deletions are accumulated as lazy Prisma promises and executed only after every SendGrid cancellation succeeds. If any request in the loop fails, execution jumps to the outer catch, no successful cancellation is removed from the database, and all subsequent reminders are skipped. The next run consequently retries already-cancelled batches as well as the failed batch, which can fail again and block the remaining reminders until they are sent. Handle failures per reminder and persist each successful cancellation independently.

findings.title: Await reminder cancellation work before returning the response
findings.body: The reminder cancellation helpers are invoked in nested forEach callbacks without awaiting their promises or including them in prismaPromises. Unlike the previous implementation, there is now no awaited database operation that deletes unscheduled reminders or durably marks scheduled emails cancelled. The request can therefore return while these essential writes and SMS cancellations are still running; in a serverless deployment they can be suspended when the response completes, leaving reminders active for a successfully cancelled booking. Collect and await these promises before completing the cancellation request.
